examples.text: Предлагаю сейчас выпить за наше знакомство.
examples.trans: I suggest we drink to our acquaintance now.

examples.text: А где твоя мама, её там нет.
examples.trans: And where is your mom, she is not there.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'disgrace' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Жалко, я твоего позора не увижу.
examples.trans: It is a pity I will not see your disgrace.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, мне очень приятно с вами познакомиться.
examples.trans: Hello, I am very pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Познакомься, сынок, это моя подруга Лариса.
examples.trans: Meet her, son, this is my friend Larisa.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'I will see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: Я просто совсем не ожидал увидеть.
examples.trans: I just did not expect to see at all.

examples.text: Стирай немедленно, пока Лена не увидела!
examples.trans: Erase it immediately before Lena sees it!

examples.text: Вот увидишь!
examples.trans: You'll see!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'in the morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я завтра утром женюсь, потом банкет.
examples.trans: I am getting married tomorrow morning, then the banquet.

examples.text: Прости, что сегодня утром так вышло.
examples.trans: Sorry that it turned out like this this morning.

examples.text: Простите, я сегодня утром в аварию попал.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I got into an accident this morning.

жениться.gloss: to marry (of a man), to get married

meanings.en: to marry (на + prepositional, of a man); to get married
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to marry (of a man), to get married'.

examples.text: Может, тебе вообще жениться больше не надо?
examples.trans: Maybe you should not get married anymore at all?

examples.text: А Даня на Нине женится!
examples.trans: And Danya will marry Nina!

examples.text: А Даня на Нине женится! И будем жить дружно и фондю есть.
examples.trans: And Danya will marry Nina! And we will live together in harmony and eat fondue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я завтра утром женюсь, потом банкет.
examples.trans: I am getting married tomorrow morning, then the banquet.

examples.text: Зачем, ты и так потрясающе выглядишь.
examples.trans: Why, you look amazing as it is.

examples.text: Может, она хочет потом квартиру себе забрать?
examples.trans: Maybe she wants to take the apartment for herself later?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'banquet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я завтра утром женюсь, потом банкет.
examples.trans: I am getting married tomorrow morning, then the banquet.

examples.text: Праздничный банкет.
examples.trans: A festive banquet.

examples.text: У нас сегодня очень важный банкет.
examples.trans: We have a very important banquet today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она машину совсем не заметила.
examples.trans: She did not notice the car at all.

examples.text: Денис, дыши спокойно, сейчас вызовем скорую.
examples.trans: Denis, breathe calmly, we will call an ambulance now.

examples.text: Всё нормально, я просто конфетой подавился.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I just choked on a candy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to place (upright)', paired with 'ставить'.

examples.text: Женись спокойно, а я поставил деньги.
examples.trans: Get married in peace, and I placed a bet.

examples.text: Поставьте ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Поставь чашку сюда.
examples.trans: Put the cup here.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Женись спокойно, а я поставил деньги.
examples.trans: Get married in peace, and I placed a bet.

examples.text: Она просит прийти лично с деньгами.
examples.trans: She asks me to come in person with the money.

examples.text: Виктор, где ты весь день ходишь?
examples.trans: Viktor, where have you been walking all day?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Денис, дыши спокойно, сейчас вызовем скорую.
examples.trans: Denis, breathe calmly, we will call an ambulance now.

examples.text: Всё нормально, я просто конфетой подавился.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, I just choked on a candy.

examples.text: Женись спокойно, а я поставил деньги.
examples.trans: Get married in peace, and I placed a bet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Виктор, ты этот тонкий намёк понял?
examples.trans: Viktor, did you understand that subtle hint?

examples.text: Ой, это просто настоящий детский сад.
examples.trans: Oh, this is just a real kindergarten.

examples.text: Атмосфера этого ресторана подкупает каждого гостя.
examples.trans: The atmosphere of this restaurant wins over every guest.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real').

examples.text: Ой, это просто настоящий детский сад.
examples.trans: Oh, this is just a real kindergarten.

examples.text: Это настоящее святое место французской кухни.
examples.trans: This is a true sacred place of French cuisine.

examples.text: Вот это всё твоё настоящее отношение, Витя!
examples.trans: That is your whole real attitude, Vitya!

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('childish, baby').

examples.text: Ой, это просто настоящий детский сад.
examples.trans: Oh, this is just a real kindergarten.

examples.text: Детские слова какие.
examples.trans: What childish words.

examples.text: Это детская комната.
examples.trans: This is the children's room.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'the park, garden' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ой, это просто настоящий детский сад.
examples.trans: Oh, this is just a real kindergarten.

examples.text: Сейчас через сад и мост — и дома.
examples.trans: Right now through the park and the bridge, and I'm home.

examples.text: Дети гуляют в городском саду.
examples.trans: The children are walking in the town park.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Завтра мы точно победим!
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will definitely win!

examples.text: Точно, тебе обязательно нужен хороший врач.
examples.trans: Exactly, you definitely need a good doctor.

examples.text: Значит, мы точно уволены, терять больше нечего.
examples.trans: That means we are definitely fired, there is nothing left to lose.

meanings.en: to defeat, to beat, to win
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'бедить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will defeat, will beat', paired with 'побеждать'.

examples.text: Завтра мы точно победим!
examples.trans: Tomorrow we will definitely win!

examples.text: Мы их всех победим!
examples.trans: We will defeat them all!

examples.text: Наша команда победила.
examples.trans: Our team won.
